problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE methods rely on panoramas, waypoint predictors, pre-built maps or hand-designed workflows and still lag far behind trained models; it is unclear how well a frontier general-purpose model can navigate directly through a minimal interface.
motivation: Understanding whether a general-purpose foundation model can navigate on its own perception, reasoning and decisions determines the role of navigation-specific training. The paper runs GPT-6-Astra in a Codex harness with only monocular RGB and primitive actions, and analyzes both scores and behaviors.
key_idea: Evaluate GPT-6-Astra zero-shot on R2R-CE through a minimal MCP observe()/step() interface in the Codex harness with monocular RGB only, and analyze its successes and failure modes.
insight: A frontier general model with a minimal interface (no map, no waypoint predictor, no panorama) can outperform both prior zero-shot systems and trained models on the 100-episode subset, so scaffolding may matter less than model capability. However, SR hides issues: 10% of successes have nDTW<50, and 15 of 24 medium-effort failures persist under ultra effort, showing that route execution and goal verification remain unreliable. The medium-vs-ultra comparison is confounded by different Codex versions.
method: Minimal interface: Codex harness sustains a continuous session; the MCP server exposes observe() (returns 512x512 monocular RGB, no action cost) and step(actions) (ordered primitive actions)
Action space: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 15°, camera tilt 30° up/down, STOP; returns execution counts and remaining budget
Model-driven decisions: GPT-6-Astra chooses when to observe, which action sequence to run and when to stop; no maps, reference paths, goal coordinates, poses or depth
Protocol: Open-Nav 100-episode R2R-CE val-unseen subset (10 scenes), 500 primitive action budget, 2400 s limit, success = STOP within 3 m, one run per episode at medium and ultra reasoning effort

Behavior analysis: instruction-type breakdown (order- vs landmark-based), nDTW on successes, action adjustments/backtracking, no-visible-change execution, stopping errors, medium vs ultra failure overlap

setting.training_data: none (no navigation-specific fine-tuning; the model's own pretraining data is undisclosed)
setting.action_space: low-level: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 15°, camera tilt 30°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE R2R-CE; simulator not named explicitly)

results: GPT-6-Astra reaches 76.0% SR / 67.9% SPL (medium) and 79.0% / 69.5% (ultra) on R2R-CE-100 with monocular RGB only. This beats the strongest zero-shot SpatialAnt (66.0 SR, panoramic plus scene reconstruction, author-sampled) by 13.0 pp and the trained Qwen-RobotNav-8B (72.1 SR, full split) by 6.9 pp, though the comparisons are on different subsets.
limitations: Only 100 episodes of R2R-CE, one run per setting, with no variance estimates; the medium/ultra runs used different Codex versions, so the reasoning-effort effect is confounded
Comparisons with baselines are not matched (subset vs full split, differing observations), and the model is proprietary so navigation-data contamination cannot be excluded
High inference cost and latency; persistent failures in route following, recovery from blocked motion and goal verification
